extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers, tax professionals, payroll administrators, employers, and tax preparers seeking to apply or interpret section 224 (qualified tips deduction)
extracted.subtask_description: Final Treasury/IRS regulations implementing section 224 of the Internal Revenue Code defining and limiting the income tax deduction for 'qualified tips', including the required list of tipped occupations, eligibility rules, limitations, and procedural requirements for claiming the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: $25,000 annual deduction limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(b)(1) limits the amount of the deduction to $25,000 for any taxable year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations clarify that this limitation applies regardless of the taxpayer's filing status and that the $25,000 maximum annual deduction for an individual or a joint return is $25,000 (i.e., applied per tax return, not per spouse). Commenters asked for per-spouse application, but the regulations retain a $25,000 per-return cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) phase-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 224(b)(2)(A), the deduction is reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 for joint returns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 224(b)(2)(B) defines MAGI for this purpose as adjusted gross income plus amounts excluded under sections 911, 931, or 933. The final regulations clarify that the MAGI phaseout is applied after applying the $25,000 limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Married filing jointly requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(f) requires that if the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), section 224 applies only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations retain the rule that married individuals must file a joint return to claim the deduction. Commenters opposing this requirement were rejected because it is statutory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid Social Security Number (SSN) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with section 224(e), to claim the deduction a taxpayer must include on the tax return a valid SSN (as defined in section 24(h)(7)) that was issued before the due date of the return (including extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxpayers with an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) rather than an SSN cannot claim the section 224 deduction. Married taxpayers must include the SSN of the taxpayer who earned the qualified tips being used; if both spouses earned qualified tips, both SSNs must be included. If a taxpayer is issued a valid SSN for the calendar year, they may use all qualified tips received in that calendar year provided the SSN is included on the return for that year. Certain noncitizens who obtain valid SSNs are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'qualified tips'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(d)(1) — 'qualified tips' means cash tips received by an individual in an occupation that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations implement the statutorily required List of Occupations that Receive Tips (TTOC). For an occupation to qualify, it must have customarily and regularly received cash tips on or before the statutory date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'cash tips'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(d)(3) defines 'cash tips' to include tips received from customers that are paid in cash or charged and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify 'cash medium of exchange' includes cash, check, credit card, debit card, gift card, tangible or intangible tokens readily exchangeable for a fixed amount in cash (e.g., casino chips), foreign currency, and electronic/mobile payment applications denominated in cash. Cash tips do not include items not exchangeable for a fixed amount in cash (event tickets, meals, services, other assets) or digital assets (as defined in section 6045(g)(3)(D) and §1.6045-1(a)(19)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary, customer-determined tips only
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips include only amounts that are paid by the customer voluntarily without any impact on the scope or cost of service or any other consequence in the event of nonpayment, are not the subject of negotiation, and are determined by the customer (section 224(d)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations explicitly exclude amounts that are not voluntary customer-determined tips from the definition of qualified tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for tips tied to illegal services
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'qualified tips' does not include tips that were received while performing a service that is a felony or misdemeanor under applicable law; amounts received for prostitution services and pornographic activity are not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, 'qualified tips' may include tips received for a service that is legal even if the establishment otherwise violates law in other respects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrebuttable presumptions recharacterizing payments as wages
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A) the employer of an employee is the payor of a cash tip received by the employee; or (B) the tip recipient has a direct ownership interest in the payor of a cash tip, there is an irrebuttable presumption that the amount paid is a recharacterization of wages or payment for services and therefore cannot be a qualified tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations provide that payments that represent a recharacterization of wages or payments for services as tips cannot be qualified tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers and supervisors receiving tip-pool amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts received by a manager or supervisor through a voluntary or mandatory tip-sharing arrangement (such as a tip pool) are not qualified tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, amounts received directly by a supervisor or manager for services provided in the course of duties performed in an occupation included on the List of Occupations that Receive Tips are qualified tips if all other regulatory requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and statements that support claiming the deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(a) allows qualified tips to be deducted if they are included on Form W-2; Form 1099-NEC; Form 1099-K; Form 1099-MISC; or Form 4137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify that statements furnished to a sole proprietorship or a single-member LLC owned by a tip recipient are considered furnished to the tip recipient owner of that entity regardless of whether the name of the sole proprietorship or LLC appears as the recipient on the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRDA and GITCA program reporting included
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees that enter a Tipped Employee Participation Agreement as part of the TRDA program or a Model Gaming Employee Tip Reporting Agreement as part of the GITCA program report tips according to tip rates established under their agreement (and these tips are included on Form W-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations clarify that 'qualified tips' for employees participating in TRDA or GITCA include tips reported using the tip rates established under their agreement and additional tips reported on Form 4137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-employed deduction limitation (net income rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with section 224(c), for self-employed taxpayers the deduction under section 224 for a trade or business is limited to the individual's net income (without regard to the section 224 deduction) from that trade or business — i.e., gross income (including qualified tips) minus deductions allocable to that trade or business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deduction cannot create or increase a loss. For a sole proprietor filing Schedule C, the deduction is limited to the amount remaining after gross income (including qualified tips) is reduced by deductions allocable to that trade or business (which would include Schedule C expenses). Whether particular deductions (self-employed health insurance, one-half of self-employment tax, retirement deduction) are allocable is beyond the scope of these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application across multiple occupations and spouses
rubrics_metrics.description: The $25,000 maximum deduction is applied per tax return and is not applied separately to different occupations for a taxpayer, or spouses in the case of spouses filing jointly, with multiple occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for how to apply the $25,000 maximum deduction limitation when claiming the deduction will be provided in income tax return instructions; these allocation instructions are beyond the scope of the regulations themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gig workers and independent contractors eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Gig workers can qualify for the deduction if their occupation is on the List of Occupations that Receive Tips and the other statutory and regulatory requirements of section 224 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because independent contractors may not receive W-2s, inclusion on the occupational list and meeting the statutory requirements matter; the final regulations note that tax return instructions and other guidance will address practical claiming questions. Transition relief for 2025 is provided in Notice 2025-69.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory list of occupations (TTOC) and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations implement the statutory requirement that the Secretary publish a List of Occupations that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024. For each occupation, the list provides a numeric Treasury Tipped Occupation Code (TTOC), an occupation title, a description of the services performed, illustrative examples, and the related Standard Occupation Classification (SOC) Code(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupations include individuals acting as assistants or apprentices to the listed occupations to the extent they perform the described services. The list is embodied in Table A (the List of Occupations that Receive Tips) with supporting descriptive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and inclusion criteria for the occupations list
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury and the IRS examined confidential tax return data (tax year 2023), GITCA and related program data, the House Budget Committee report, DOL FLSA guidance and caselaw, and PSID survey data to identify occupations that 'customarily and regularly' received cash tips on or before December 31, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on FLSA guidance and the record, occupations had to have received cash tips more often than occasionally during a calendar year ending on or before December 31, 2024 to be considered. The agencies rejected using SOC codes alone or tax return data alone because each alternative either included occupations that did not customarily receive tips or omitted occupations (e.g., independent contractors) that did.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical metrics used in Table A
rubrics_metrics.description: Table A summarizes Tax Year 2023 taxpayer information for single-job holders: percentage with at least $100 of tips reported on Form W-2 or Form 4137; percent of all reported tips from the related SOC code(s); and reported tips as a percent of wage compensation for tipped workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics support the occupation listings and provide empirical context for inclusion decisions (examples: 82.8% of bartenders had at least $100 of tips reported; reported tips were 63.4% of wages for bartenders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and reliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations apply for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Taxpayers may rely on the proposed regulations for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024 and on or before the date the final regulations are published, provided taxpayers follow the proposed regulations in their entirety and consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective period for the statute's deduction is noted (for taxable years beginning after Dec 31, 2024 and before Jan 1, 2029).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision in this rulemaking is held to be invalid or unenforceable facially, or as applied to any person or circumstance, it shall be severable from the remainder of this rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A severability clause preserves the remainder of the rulemaking and its application to persons/circumstances not affected by the invalidated provision.
